subject: Request: Keystore segregation, subnet egress map, and CAIQ evidence for EU-hosted workloads
messages:
From: Marta Gomez <security@clinix.com>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Ayers <procurement@clinix.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: CAIQ / SIG items: keystore separation + subnet-level egress map (EU)

Hi Lukas,

Thanks for the call today. As we discussed, Clinix needs a short evidence package to finish our SIG/CAIQ review and confirm we can host sensitive workloads in your EU region. Specifically we're asking for the following items for EU-hosted workloads (primary requirements first):

1) Keystore / key separation: description of how customer data keys are segregated per-tenant and per-region, whether CMK (customer-managed KMS) support is available, and a sketch of envelope key flow for redactable PII.

2) Subnet-level egress mapping: network diagram or table showing which subnets/nodes in the EU cluster can egress to third-party services, peering endpoints (Privatelink/Peering IDs), and the controls (SG/ACL) that enforce that.

3) Audit / log retention for EU nodes: retention windows and an outline of the audit trail (who/what/where) for KMS operations and VPC flow logs.

4) CAIQ pointers / SIG redlines: an annotated CAIQ spreadsheet (we attached our Clinix_SIG.xlsx) highlighting gaps and any compensating controls. If you can ship a short mapping to your SOC 2 controls that would help procurement speed things up.

Can you confirm whether you can provide a deliverable set (network diagram, keystore separation doc, annotated CAIQ) within 5 business days? We may request a redacted internal diagram for procurement. Also let us know if a brief technical call (30m) with your infra owner is required.

Thanks,
Marta
Marta Gomez
Director, Security Operations
Clinix Health
security@clinix.com

Attachment: Clinix_SIG.xlsx (spreadsheet, 120KB)

From: Lukas Meyer <lukas@redwood.com>
To: Marta Gomez <security@clinix.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 10:07:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: CAIQ / SIG items: keystore separation + subnet-level egress map (EU)

Hi Marta — thanks for the clear list. We're able to provide the items you've requested. High level plan and owners below:

- Deliverables (initial package within 72 hours):
  * redwood_keystore_separation_v1.pdf — per-region keystore segregation and envelope flow (covers CMK options, HSM-backed flows, and tenant separation model).
  * vpc_diagram.png — subnet and peering topology for the EU cluster, annotated with peering ids and private endpoint references.
  * residency_matrix.csv — audit/log retention and SOC2 control mapping for EU nodes.

- Owners: Sean Gallagher (cc'd) will own the network/peering diagram and subnet egress mapping. Rachel Kim will coordinate legal artifacts and handle redaction/DocuSign for the DPA. I'll own the keystore and CMK notes.

A couple quick clarifications that will help us scope the diagrams:
1) Do you need IP-level egress lists to specific third-party SaaS endpoints, or is a high-level destination classification (payment providers, telemetry vendors, identity providers) enough?
2) For CMK: do you require complete customer-managed KMS (no Redwood access) or a bring-your-own-key (BYOK) envelope flow with rotation managed by Clinix? We support both — we'll note tradeoffs.

We'll produce a redacted diagram suitable for procurement and a separate full internal operator diagram marked as \"for-ops-only\" if you require it. I'll aim to get the initial artifacts uploaded to a shared folder by end of day Wednesday.

Best,
Lukas Meyer
Head of Solutions Engineering — Redwood Inference
lukas@redwood.com

Attachments (to send): redwood_keystore_separation_v1.pdf; residency_matrix.csv; vpc_diagram.png

Subject: Re: CAIQ / SIG items: keystore separation + subnet-level egress map (EU)

Marta — looping in operational detail. Quick answers to Lukas' clarifying questions:

1) Egress specificity: we can provide both a high-level classification and an optional IP-level allowlist for SaaS integrations. For regulatory reviewers we usually include destination CIDR blocks for third-party peering and note which flows traverse the public internet vs. Private Peering.

2) CMK model: Redwood supports three models:
   - Redwood-managed KMS (default, HSM-backed, access limited to automated operator roles)
   - Customer-managed KMS (BYOK with Cloud KMS; we never hold plaintext CMK)
   - Hybrid envelope model (customer rotates DEKs, Redwood stores envelope metadata; recommended when you want key autonomy + service convenience)

We'll include a short matrix that maps each model to operational impacts (audit retention, backup/restore, key-rotation responsibilities).

I'll attach an operator diagram (vpc_diagram.png) with subnets labeled and a CSV for per-subnet egress policies. Expect the initial package in ~48 hours; if you want the IP-level lists we'll need another day to sanitize and redact any internal ranges.

Sean Gallagher
Senior Infrastructure Engineer — Redwood Inference
sean@redwood.com
